# HLBuilder

HLBuilder is an open-source visual planner for homelabs, LAN parties and game servers. You draw the network and get the IP plan, hardware sizing and config files. It plans a network before it is built; it does not scan or monitor one.

Canonical site: https://hlbldr.com/
Sitemap: https://hlbldr.com/sitemap.xml

## What HLBuilder does

HLBuilder lets you drag routers, switches, servers, NAS devices and single-board computers onto a canvas and wire them together. It assigns IP addresses from the topology, adds up CPU, memory, storage and power, and generates Docker Compose, Ansible and reverse proxy files.

- Guided planner for three kinds of project: homelab, LAN party, game server.
- LAN party: tables and seats, DHCP pool sized for the players, load on every power circuit.
- Game servers: Minecraft, Valheim, Palworld, Counter-Strike 2, Factorio and more, sized per player, with ports and a Compose file per host.
- Built-in MCP server and an optional bring-your-own-key assistant. An LLM can only propose changes; the owner applies them.
- Free and open source (AGPL-3.0). Hosted at https://hlbldr.com/ or self-hosted with Docker Compose.
- Source: https://github.com/Butterski/homelab-builder

## Product facts

- The frontend is a React and Vite app.
- The backend is a Go API.
- The IPAM service calculates network assignments from saved topology data.
- The homepage and the docs under /docs/ are static HTML and can be read without running JavaScript.
- Shared build URLs are user-generated and should not be indexed.
